title: [WT-10] Wrappers: quality gate on the merged tree under the land lease
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §2.2 (L3, L6, L14) and §2.3.

Objective: when settings.qualityGate applies, main is updated only after the gate passes on the exact merged tree that will land (epic rail 1). Seats of this project serialize through one daemon lease, so the gate rarely re-runs under contention.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- L3, only when a gate will run: acquire_resource on `git-land-<target>` (every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by '-', at most 64 chars), then wait_for_resource until granted, bounded by MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC (default 1800). A timeout or RPC failure gives MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE and lands nothing (record failed; WT-11 adds the route with reason contention).
- L6: the existing freeze_candidate B M + run_frozen_gate (New-MoeFrozenCandidate / Invoke-MoeFrozenGate), fed the merged tree M with parent B. Failure gives the existing MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE and lands nothing (WT-11 adds the route with reason gate).
- Under the lease at most 2 L4-L10 attempts, each re-running the gate on the new merge.
- L14: release_resource on every path, including failures and the exit trap.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-09 (task-0921d6d76a6b40a685077245b19ac639).

NOT in scope: declaring the resource in settings (the §7.3 runbook); the unlanded route (WT-11); shared-mode gate behaviour, which stays unchanged; docs (WT-17/WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): with a qualityGate, the gate's frozen commit has tree M (the merge of B and T) and parent B; a passing gate lands C, a failing gate prints MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE and leaves main unchanged.
postflight case: the fake proxy sees acquire_resource for git-land-main before the gate and release_resource after, on both the pass and the fail path; with no qualityGate no lease call is made.
postflight case: a lease wait past MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC prints MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE and lands nothing.
bash scripts/tests/worktree-landing.sh still passes unchanged; existing shared-mode gate cases pass unchanged.
Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes; the verification command exits 0 and postflight.ps1 passes on a Windows seat.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Bind the landed producer interfaces and add deterministic lease fixtures. Re-read WT-S comments, WT-09 landing rounds, WT-10G and WT-10P source/hand-offs after their structural dependencies are satisfied; do not write a second landing engine or emulate missing prerequisites. G's declared contract is `run_frozen_gate worktree` / `Invoke-MoeFrozenGate ... -WorktreeMode`; P's new wrapper-only contract is absolute Unix-ms MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS bounding the entire one-shot proxy call, including connect/EOF. Confirm the selected built proxy contains that fix before testing a queued wait. Preserve shared-mode default call signatures. In the existing fake proxy, add narrowly opt-in worktree lease scenarios and log acquire_resource/wait_for_resource/release_resource in order together with existing candidate/check/ledger events. Model granted with lease identity, queued then granted, repeated timedOut, daemon refusal/malformed response, withheld reply until proxy deadline, and release failure once then success. Validate caller taskId/workerId and exact resource id; default fixture modes must not change. No test may pretend granted:false is success. Use persisted fixture counters per temp project, not process-local counters (every RPC gets a fresh process).
implementationPlan.note: Fake proxy now models acquire_resource/wait_for_resource/release_resource (daemon reply shapes from tools/acquireResource.ts, waitForResource.ts, releaseResource.ts). Every call is logged to evidence-rpcs.jsonl in order, with the MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS it carried. Checks: caller task and worker must match the claimed attempt, resource must equal FAKE_LEASE_RESOURCE (default git-land-main), timeoutMs must be 1000..600000, no force, and ifAcquiredAt must name the held grant. Grants persist in .moe/resources/<id>.json. FAKE_LEASE_MODE values: unset (grant), queued, timeout, late, withheld (honours the proxy deadline, then exits 1), refuse, malformed (granted:"true"), release-fail-once (counted from the RPC log). The default mode only adds handlers: no wrapper called these tools before. Smoke-tested each mode directly against a temp project. Pre-existing dirty .moe/roles, .moe/skills and .moe/tasks paths belong to other sessions and were left alone.

implementationPlan.description:
2. Implement L3 acquire/wait in both worktree completion arms, with tests first (DoD 2–3). Separate raw configured qualityGate from the scope-filtered command. A configured gate means take the lease even on a mid-epic/scope-skipped completion; absent/blank gate means no lease RPC. Checkpoints/shared mode make no new lease calls. Introduce acquire_land_lease / Acquire-MoeLandLease (new helpers) and per-landing resource/attempted/granted/lease-generation state. Resource identity is the complete `git-land-` + target string with every character outside ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._-] replaced by '-', then truncated to 64 total characters; test slash, Unicode and long targets. Parse MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC as a positive bounded numeric duration, default 1800 when unset; invalid/zero/negative/overflow input fails closed with MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE before a resource RPC. Establish one overall deadline before acquire. Supply the actual landing task and worker, never create a synthetic task or use report_blocked during finalization. Call acquire_resource; only literal granted:true admits L4. For granted:false, call wait_for_resource repeatedly with timeoutMs=min(600000, remaining budget), never request below its 1000ms minimum (expire instead). Continue only a genuine timedOut response while budget remains; cancelled/error/malformed/RPC failure fails closed. Set P's one-shot deadline env to the same overall deadline for each call and restore it afterward (PS try/finally, Bash per-call env), so a hung/not-connected proxy cannot exceed the configured bound. A grant returned after the deadline is not admission: release it and fail. Example invariant:
```text
if !configuredGate: return admitted_without_lease
attempted = true
reply = acquire(resource, realTask, realWorker, absoluteDeadline)
while reply.granted !== true and reply is queued/timedOut and remaining >= 1000ms:
    reply = wait(resource, realTask, realWorker, min(600000, remaining), absoluteDeadline)
if reply.granted !== true or deadline_expired: LAND_CODE=MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE; fail
```
Both postflight harnesses must show acquire before any gate/publication, queued grant after a delay greater than the old two-second proxy cutoff, scope-skipped gate still acquires, no configured gate makes no lease call, timeout/non-answer/refusal prints the code with main unchanged and no candidate/gate/push, and no successful completion row is recorded. Use short test budgets and fake replies, not a real 30-minute wait.
implementationPlan.note: L3 in both wrappers. sh: land_lease_id/land_lease_budget/land_lease_rpc/land_lease_read/acquire_land_lease. ps1: Get-MoeLandLeaseId/Get-MoeLandLeaseBudget/Invoke-MoeLandLeaseRpc/Request-MoeLandLease. One deadline; each RPC gets MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS as a per-call prefix (sh) or set/restore (ps1), never exported. Bad MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC refused before any RPC. Tests first (RED seen: 'no function land_lease_id', and old MOE_COMMIT_FAILED instead of MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE): lease-units (slash/Unicode/astral/long ids, budget parser), wt-lease-fails (timeout/withheld/late/refuse/malformed/budget/disabled), no-lease asserts added to wt-completion and wt-fails; the fake's queued grant now comes after 2.5s. Mutation check (scratch copy outside the checkout) caught each broken line, including the dropped per-call deadline, an accepted late grant and a lease taken without a gate. 17 dirty paths from other sessions/debris left untouched.

implementationPlan.description: 3. Implement L14 cleanup and failure-safe resource ownership (DoD 2–3). Introduce idempotent release_land_lease / Release-MoeLandLease and invoke it after every worktree completion return path plus cleanup_temp/PowerShell outer finally, before deregistration and before clearing the landing identity. Mark acquisition attempted before sending the RPC so an ambiguous reply still cancels this task's queue/lease. Release only this resource + original task + worker, never force and never another task; when the granted lease's acquiredAt is known, use the existing release preconditions to avoid releasing a later lease generation. Queue-only cleanup uses the existing task-scoped release behavior. Give cleanup its own short bounded proxy deadline (5 seconds), restoring the environment afterward. Clear ownership state only after an acknowledged release; a failed release warns MOE_LAND_LEASE_RELEASE_FAILED and remains eligible for one exit-trap retry. Cleanup failure must not overwrite a known published/failed landing outcome or rerun a publication; daemon lease expiry/releaseOnDeregister remains a backstop, not a successful-release claim. Preserve existing signal deferral across publication/recording from WT-08/09; a handled exit before publication releases and preserves T. Mirrored tests assert release after passing and failing gate, after lease timeout/ambiguous acquire, after merge/publication failure, and on a handled exit while queued/gating; never publish on a missing grant. Test release failure then cleanup retry without a duplicate committed ledger row. SIGKILL cannot run a trap: do not claim otherwise.
implementationPlan.note: L14 in both wrappers. release_land_lease / Release-MoeLandLease: the ps1 helpers are renamed to the plan's Acquire-/Release-MoeLandLease (they were Request-/Clear-MoeLandLease in the step-2 note). The in-band release is one call that every return path reaches: sh after the outcome block, ps1 in the finally. It runs after the completion row/finalize and before the summary and the loop's identity reset. cleanup_temp and the ps1 outer finally retry it once before deregister. The lease state is set before the acquire RPC, so an ambiguous or late reply still releases. Each release names the stored resource+task+worker (never the current task) and never forces. It is pinned with ifAcquiredAt when the grant's acquiredAt is a string, else task-scoped. It has its own 5s per-call deadline: sh uses a per-call prefix, ps1 sets and restores it in try/finally. State clears only on an answered release. A failure warns MOE_LAND_LEASE_RELEASE_FAILED, keeps the state and never rewrites the outcome. NEW: before a new acquire replaces the state, an earlier landing's failed release gets its one retry. Without it, a looping wrapper's next landing would drop that retry. Tests (postflight-worktree.cjs, run by postflight.sh and .ps1): wt-gate covers release after a pass, a failing gate and a .moe-writing gate. In wt-gate's release-fail-once run, the in-band release fails, the exit retry succeeds, there is exactly one committed row and holders are []. wt-lease-fails covers timeout/withheld/late/refuse/malformed plus a NEW merge-tree failure row; each releases with main unchanged and no gate. wt-lease-signal (sh only) covers queued plus a NEW gating variant: a SIGTERM while the gate runs means one gate run, main unchanged, T keeps its bytes, and acquire then release. NEW lease-retry case (both engines): the old task's pinned release comes before the new acquire, and a failed retry warns while the new lease proceeds. RED, on scratch copies outside the checkout: lease-retry fails without the retry line (bash and PS 5.1). The merge row and the gating variant fail with both release sites removed. GREEN on bash: lease-units, lease-retry, wt-lease-fails, wt-lease-signal, wt-gate, wt-completion, wt-fails, codes all ok; bash -n ok; parity PASS. Native Windows (cmd.exe -> Windows node, launched from WSL), PS 5.1: lease-units, lease-retry, wt-lease-fails, wt-gate, wt-completion, wt-fails, codes ok; wt-lease-signal n/a (no signal on Windows). pwsh 7: lease-units, lease-retry, wt-lease-fails, wt-gate ok. BOM kept, LF kept. Not claimed: SIGKILL runs no trap, and the sh hot-reload exec skips it, so a pending failed release is lost there; lease expiry or the task leaving active status is the backstop. Net task diff is now 390 LOC. The 17 other-session dirty paths are untouched.

implementationPlan.description: 4. Insert L6 on each fresh merged candidate and enforce round budgets (DoD 1,4). Consume WT-09's existing round after L5/L5b and before L7/L8/L9. Keep T fixed, derive fresh B/M each round, and call `freeze_candidate "$B" "$M"` then `run_frozen_gate worktree`; PS uses `New-MoeFrozenCandidate $Git $M $B`, existing Send-MoeCandidate, then `Invoke-MoeFrozenGate $Git $Frozen $command -WorktreeMode`. Candidate/check and journal must name this exact M and parent B, never pre-merge task T or control HEAD. Preserve evidence-refusal error handling: freeze/evidence/gate/sparse/integrity failure is MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE, retains the existing failed+rescue path, releases, and never publishes. WT-11 later adds outcome unlanded/reason gate/contention; do not implement it here. If the effective gate runs, allow at most TWO L4-L9 rounds under one lease and rerun the gate for the new merged pair on every retry, with no stale result reuse. If scope skips the gate, preserve THREE ungated rounds but still lease when a gate is configured; if none is configured preserve the existing no-lease three-round behavior. Keep remote unknown-outcome/journal and non-forced push rules unchanged. Do not let MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE bypass an applicable worktree-mode configured gate: refuse safely before publication; shared-mode opt-out is unchanged. Twin tests use non-overlapping peer/task hunks to prove frozen HEAD^{tree}=M and HEAD^=B, published C^{tree}=M and C^=B; a gate reads both hunks and no .moe. A failing gate and a gate creating .moe/x leave main unchanged and release; the latter includes MOE_WORKTREE_GATE_INTEGRITY. Force one target race: second gate sees new B/M, then succeeds; force two losses: contention failure with exactly two gate runs and no task publication. Existing shared gate and WT-08T tests remain unchanged.

What I checked:
- Grant checks: only a literal granted:true for this task's lease is accepted. granted:"true", a refusal, a cancellation, a missing answer or a malformed reply all give MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_LAND_LEASE (wt-lease-fails covers refuse, malformed and withheld).
- Grant at the deadline: a grant that arrives after the single deadline fails, and the lease is released pinned to its acquiredAt (case "late"). Wait timeouts use timeoutMs = min(600000, time left), and the loop stops when less than 1s is left.
- No-answer proxy: every proxy call carries MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS, an absolute deadline, so no call can wait past the caller's deadline (case "withheld").
- Lost acquire reply: fails closed, followed by a release scoped to this task.
- Lost release reply: prints the warning MOE_LAND_LEASE_RELEASE_FAILED and keeps its state for one retry. The retry happens at the next acquire, or else in the sh exit trap or the ps1 outer finally (lease-retry, release-fail-once).
- Waiter that became the holder before cleanup: covered by the release scoped to this task.
- Another task's lease: never released, since the release requires both the precondition and the taskId and never uses force.
- Env leaks: none. sh sets the deadline per call; ps1 sets and restores it in a finally block.
- Cleanup: the release never changes the landing outcome, so it can't turn a confirmed remote publication into a failure.
- Exact M/B: the frozen and gated commit has tree M and parent B, and C = commit-tree M -p B is what gets journaled and published (wt-gate race: the gate ran [M0,B] and then [M1,peer]; C^ = peer and C^{tree} = M1).
- Rounds: 2 with a gate, 3 without, and every merge after contention is gated again.
- .moe: the worktree runner never materializes it; the integrity case gives MOE_WORKTREE_GATE_INTEGRITY.
- Scoped-but-configured gates: CS_QUALITY_GATE / configuredGate apply only in worktree landing. There, MOE_DISABLE_QUALITY_GATE=1 is refused with MOE_COMMIT_FAILED_GATE instead of skipping the gate.
- Shared mode: unchanged.
- Held-out tests: worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} are unchanged versus 8ad04de7.
- Encoding: the ps1 BOM and LF line endings are kept, and bash -n passes.
- No peer dirt was staged.

Mutants: I tried 6 on bash and 6 on PS 5.1 (gate on T's tree, always 3 rounds, no worktree arm, parent T, gate only in round 1, DISABLE refusal dropped). All 12 were killed, and the unmutated controls passed.

Theoretical notes for QA, no fix needed:
1. A SIGTERM sent only to the wrapper (not its process group) during a long wait_for_resource is handled after the RPC returns. That takes at most 600s and is bounded by the deadline. A terminal Ctrl+C also hits the proxy, which exits within 2s.
2. The sh hot-reload exec and SIGKILL lose a pending failed release. Lease expiry is the backstop.
3. A pinned retry of a release whose reply was lost warns twice, which is harmless.
4. On a Linux seat with a non-UTF-8 locale, land_lease_id may compute a different id for a non-ASCII target name.

The documentation and resource declaration, and the migration flags, stay with their named later tasks.

comments.content:
Contract correction from the WT-S revision after QA reject 1. Where this comment and the row's description differ, the revised docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md and this comment win. Plan against revised §2.2 (L3/L6/L14), §2.3 and §7.3.

1. Take the lease on EVERY completion landing, not "only when a gate will run".
   - Acquire, wait, release and the bounds are unchanged.
   - Rounds are L4-L9: at most 3 without a gate, 2 with one.

2. Gate worktree arm (rail 3):
   - Add the gate worktree with `--no-checkout`. Never pass `core.sparseCheckout=false`.
   - Then run `sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' '!/.moe/'` and `read-tree -mu HEAD`.
   - The integrity helper is gate_integrity_wt / Test-MoeGateIntegrityWorktree:
     - keep the HEAD and write-tree checks;
     - clear assume-unchanged and skip-worktree bits only outside `.moe/`;
     - require a clean diff-files;
     - fail with MOE_WORKTREE_GATE_INTEGRITY when `<gate>/.moe` exists, before or after the command. That makes the landing unlanded `gate`.
   - Shared mode keeps today's run_frozen_gate / gate_integrity unchanged (rail 4).
   - Cases:
     - a gate command that creates `.moe/x` → integrity failure, nothing published;
     - `.moe` is absent while the command runs;
     - the shared-mode gate behaves as before.

3. Migration landing `--land-branch <branch>` / `-LandBranch <branch>` (§7.3):
   - Sequence: L3, then rounds of:
     - L4;
     - L5 `merge-tree --write-tree B <branch>`;
     - L6 on exactly M;
     - L7 C = `commit-tree M -p B -p <branch tip>`;
     - L9 and L10.
     Then L14.
   - L6 always runs settings.qualityGate, whatever qualityGateScope says. With no gate set, refuse with MOE_MIGRATION_NO_GATE before any fetch.
   - Skip L0-L2, L5b, L8 and L11-L13. Record no Candidate, CheckRun or ledger row.
   - These publish nothing: a conflict, a failed gate, a lease timeout, 2 exhausted rounds.
   - An unknown outcome stops. Once main contains the branch, a re-run exits 0 with MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT.
   - Cases: clean landing, conflict, no-gate refusal, re-run idempotence.

If this exceeds taskSizing at plan time, split item 3 into its own row (SPIDR, Interface) and make WT-16 depend on it.

comments.content:
Follow-up to the WT-S revision comment above. It narrows that comment's item 1 so it matches this row's DoD2 (definitionOfDone is human-owned). Revised §2.2 L3 and §2.3 now say the same:
- While `settings.qualityGate` is set, take the land lease on every completion landing, whether or not this landing's `qualityGateScope` runs the gate. This stops an ungated peer from publishing while a gated landing is gating.
- With no `qualityGate` set, make no lease call, exactly as DoD2 says.

comments.author: architect-899a90d6
comments.content:
The proxy contract from WT-10P (task-b5a176355a7c443d98952466b409f941, plan rev 1, now WORKING). Build against these exact semantics; read the landed proxy bytes before relying on the text.

1. `MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS` is an absolute Unix epoch in ms, plain decimal digits forming a safe integer.
   - Unset or blank means no bound, so a PS restore can blank it.
   - Any other invalid value fails closed: one JSON-RPC error with id null, 'Invalid MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS: <reason>', then exit 1 without connecting.
2. When the deadline expires (during connect, queued, sent or the EOF drain):
   - One error per known pending id: 'Proxy deadline exceeded (MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS)'. A null-id error is written when no id is known yet (the proxy never connected).
   - Then exit 1, with no late success and no reconnect.
3. The long EOF drain applies only to a session that never sent MCP `initialize`. moe_rpc and Invoke-MoeRpc must keep piping one bare tools/call.
   - A pending wait_for_resource then drains until its daemon reply or sentAt + MOE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_MS (default 660000).
   - Keep timeoutMs at 600000 or less, so the daemon's own timedOut reply wins.
4. A daemon socket lost mid-drain errors at once with 'Connection to daemon lost before response received'.
   - That path, and the 2s grace paths, still exit 0 with an error line, exactly as today. Decide on the reply's result or error, never on the exit code alone.
   - SIGINT/SIGTERM cap any drain at 2s.
